content_html_sanitized:
I have previously written about the different ways that cannabis is used and how they are connected.

See

Massive New Study of California Cannabis Users Shows Continuum Between Recreational and Medical Use.

And

Recreational, Sacramental and Medical: Why There’s No Clear Delineation Between Recreational and Medical Cannabis.

 

In earlier times and in different cultures there would not necessarily have been any real distinction between the religious and the medical. If someone was sick, it would have been perfectly logical to go to a shaman who might also use plants that have psychoactive properties. (The pejorative term “Witch Doctor” made the connection clear.)

 

However, as “modern medicine” replaced incantation with “scientific” jargon patients were still left with words that they didn’t understand.

 

Then along came medical “marijuana” (foreign word) containing hundreds of compounds that no one understood that worked in ways that no one understands, and had been “demonized”.

 

The Witch Doctor was a bureaucrat with a gun. The incantation was  “You are under arrest”.

 

“Medicine” was no longer a plant that helped the sick to get well. It was a ritual that had to be sponsored by the government, that the government would not sponsor.

 

Consequently, patients were on their own, and when they were free to try cannabis, they “self medicated”. So, now we see the “latest research” showing marijuana use is “linked to” all sorts of health problems.

 

For example, the “hangover”, A.K.A., alcohol withdrawal, is very familiar to millions of people around the world. In 1967, I discovered cannabis alleviates its symptoms. (I think I should get a Nobel Prize for medicine.)

 

Apparently, others have also, because cannabis is widely used for that purpose. How wonderful, but cannabis use is now “linked to” the problems caused by alcohol addiction. So now alcoholics also have “Cannabis Use Disorder” because they can’t quit using cannabis.

From 1998, Lungren Believes People Dying Of Alcoholism Should Be Able To Smoke Tobacco in Bars

But Not Marijuana in Hospices

(We’ve come a long way, baby! Believe it or not. That line used to be a slogan for a cigarette brand marketed to women.)

 

And as the  population ages more and more seniors are self medicating with cannabis.

See AMA Reports More Seniors Using Marijuana. Maybe It’s Because Common Drugs That They Prescribe Are Tied to Increased Risk of Cognitive Decline In Seniors But Marijuana Helps.

 

In the meantime, what should patients tell their doctors about their cannabis use?

See The Relevance of “Set and Setting” for Medical Cannabis Patients in a Hostile Environment

 

How can cannabis be integrated into modern medicine after the medical establishment has opposed it for decades?
